title: Traditional Crafts in the 21st Century
source: Adapted from a cultural feature in the 'Hong Kong Heritage' journal (January 2026).
topic_description: A feature story highlights a young 'Z-generation' artisan who is utilizing 3D printing technology to recreate and preserve the intricate art of traditional Chinese wood carving. While some applaud this 'tech-traditional fusion' as the only way to save dying cultures, traditionalists argue that removing the human hand from the process strips the craft of its soul and authenticity.
discussion_points: The intrinsic value of traditional crafts in an increasingly high-tech and automated world.
The role of modern technology, such as 3D printing and VR, in documenting and saving dying cultures.
Effective ways to make traditional artisanal careers more attractive to modern, tech-savvy students.
Any other related ideas you think are important.

candidates.A: The Agreement/Linker (Social Goal: The Elaborator): Focuses on revitalization through innovation. Uses Signposting Phrases like 'From a cultural perspective...' and 'From a commercial standpoint...'. Mentions HK examples like digital preservation of neon signs or traditional tailoring.
candidates.B: The Counter/Nuance (Social Goal: The Pragmatist): Highlights loss of 'authenticity'. Uses Signposting Phrases like 'If we look at this from an artistic perspective...'. **Authenticity Argument**: B should challenge A: 'If a machine carves the wood, are we preserving the skill or just the final product? Isn't the human struggle part of the value?'
candidates.C: The Facilitator/Timer (Social Goal: The Synthesizer): Merges views with explicit categorization. Uses Signposting Phrases like 'Candidate A values accessibility, while B prioritizes the human touch.' **Hybrid Career Argument**: Regarding attractiveness, C should propose: 'Perhaps we don't need students to be full-time carvers. Could they be "Tech-Artisans" who spend half their time in a digital lab and half in a traditional studio? This Slashie model might be more sustainable.'
candidates.D: The AI Examiner instructions: Look for Semantic Analysis where students signpost their arguments (Cultural, Artistic, Economic, Social). Specifically check for: 'Authenticity vs. Efficiency' and 'Tangible vs. Intangible Heritage'. For IR #3, credit students who propose a hybrid approach (e.g., 'Digital Craftsman').

individual_response_questions: Do you like visiting old neighborhoods?
What is your favorite local tradition?
If your school offered a wood-carving class instead of a coding class, which would you choose and why?
Do you think handmade items are more valuable than machine-made ones?
